newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Sept 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Sept 5.

text.p: PRAVO - The Czech government, conscious of the unusual gravity of the situation surrounding Kreditni Banka's bankruptcy, entrusted Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik, Justice Minister Jan Kalvoda and Interior Minister Jan Ruml with an investigation of the matter.
- Michael Jackson's Saturday concert on Prague's Letna Plain, should bring approximately 60 million crowns to the state's coffers through VAT charges.

- The Czech army will have to cut back on some investments, especially in the area of modernisation. While the army planned to receive 12 billion crowns yearly, the figure is likely to be 6.3 billion crowns this year and a similar amount in 1997.

- The recent decision by the Czech government to cut spending by five percent across the board will mean a decrease of 965 million crowns for the Ministry of Transport according to minister Martin Riman. The result will be reduced investment, especially in the repair of highways.
- A contract for cooperation between Vychodoslovenske Zelezarny (VSZ), Trinecke Zelezarny and Moravia Steel was recently signed in the East Slovak town of Kosice.

- The Dutch company Tebodin B.V. has purchased a major share in the Prague-based Projekta. While Tebodin purchased less than 50 percent, the company's share is expected to exceed that figure within one year.

- The largest trade deficit in the first seven months of this year was with Russia with a deficit of 20.1 billion crowns. This is followed by Italy with a 13.8 billion-crown deficit, France at 8.5 billion crowns and Britain at approximately eight billion crowns.
- Countries of the Central European Free Trade Agreement should lower trade barriers faster, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus stated during a government session on Wednesday.
- Banka Hana announced that at the end of October the bank is planning to issue stock to increase its basic capital by 499.2 million crowns to 1.999 billion crowns. This is the bank's ninth issue.
- Belgian's supranational glass company Glaverbel purchased the remaining 27 percent of the shares in Glavunion from Sklo Union, giving it 100 percent ownership of the company.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - According to experts from the International Atomic Energy Agency, the Temelin Nuclear power Plant is safe.

- Skoda Plzen and Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka (CSOB) are discussing an agreement for the sale of a decisive share in Mokotov a.s., formerly a foreign trade company. Currently 51 percent of the company is owned by FINOP Holding a.s., which in turn is owned by CSOB.
